blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Recent advances in gigapixel-level imaging have brought High-Resolution Wide shots to the forefront of research. However, these images present significant challenges: extreme sparsity of foreground, gigapixel-level resolutions and interleaving of foreground and background. This causes traditional detectors and attention mechanisms to be hindered by background, resulting in inefficiency and inaccuracy. To tackle this problem, we propose BiHashFormer, a dual sparsified branch transformer built on hashing. RoI Selector will predict the foreground proportion for top-k selecting target-containing windows. The compression branch processes windows selected and refines attention into HashAttention by discarding half of the key-value pairs, reducing cost and improving efficiency. The compensation branch uses HashMiner to perform low-cost hash searches in the remaining regions, recovering features of missed objects. Experiments confirm that the selection relationship in HashAttention is one-way and reveal the preference of different queries for keys. In experiments on the gigapixel benchmark PANDA, BiHashFormer reduces 37.5% backbone FLOPs while improving AP50 to 81.0%. Moreover, this parallel dual-branch structure allows the model to avoid inference delays caused by inter-branch dependencies, while achieving much greater stability than single-branch models, specially with low rates of RoI selection.
blocks.zh: 最近千兆像素级成像工作的进展,使高分辨率宽镜头成为研究的前沿。 然而,这些图像带来了重大挑战:前地的极端伸缩、千兆像素级分辨率以及前地和背景的交接。 这导致传统的探测器和注意机制受到背景的阻碍,导致效率低下和不准确。 为了解决这一问题,我们建议波黑铸币局(BHAHashFORmer),一个以散列为主的双螺旋分枝变压器。 RoI 选择器将预测顶端- k 选择目标窗口的前景比例 。 压缩分支处理窗口通过丢弃一半的密钥值对,降低成本并提高效率来选择和完善注意力入HashAtthy. 补偿处利用Hashminer在其余区域进行低成本散列搜索,恢复被丢失物体的特征. 实验证实HashAttenty中的选择关系是单向的,并揭示了不同查询键的偏好. 在千兆像素基准PANDA的实验中,波黑Former将骨干FLOP降低37.5%,同时将AP50提高到81.0%. 此外,这种平行的双分支结构使模型能够避免由分支间依赖引起的推论延迟,同时实现比单分支模型更大的稳定性,特别是RoI选择率低.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: In computer vision, object detection has long been recognized as a central challenge, requiring algorithms to simultaneously determine the location and category of target instances within an image. The standard output of such systems usually consists of a bounding box together with a class label. Landmark approaches, exemplified by Fast R-CNN [ 13 ] , have achieved notable success on large-scale benchmarks such as MS COCO [ 5 ] . More recently, advances in nondestructive imaging have shifted attention toward High-Resolution Wide (HRW) detection [ 3 , 3 ] . This setting involves analyzing imagery with both extremely fine spatial detail and expansive coverage, posing unique computational and modeling challenges. Representative scenarios include gigapixel drone photography [ 25 ] , satellite-based observation [ 12 , 9 , 8 ] , and panoramic camera data [ 4 ] .
blocks.zh: 在计算机视觉中,物体检测早已被公认为一个中心挑战,需要算法同时确定一个图像中的目标实例的位置和类别. 此类系统的标准输出通常由一个有分界的框和一个类标签组成. 以快速R-CNN[13]为范例的地标方法在MS COCO等大规模基准方面取得了显著成功. 最近,非破坏性成像的进展将注意力转移到高分辨率宽度探测[3、3]。 这种背景包括分析具有极其细微的空间细节和广度的图像,从而构成独特的计算和建模挑战。 具有代表性的情景包括:Giapixel无人机摄影[25]、卫星观测[12、9、8]和全景相机数据。 [4].

blocks.en: The first problem in HRW detection is that the objects we care about only take up a very small part of the whole picture. In normal detection datasets, the foreground can cover more than half of the image. But in HRW scenes, the foreground is usually less than 15% [ 4 ] , because the images come from large real-world views that naturally include wide areas of background such as sky, buildings, or trees. This means detectors have to search through a lot of background to find a few targets, and even strong models like DINO [ 14 ] , Deformable DETR [ 35 ] , and RMT [ 12 ] often make mistakes when the background is too dominant. This problem is illustrated by Figure 1 .
blocks.zh: 人权观察发现的第一个问题是,我们所关心的物体只占整个画面的很小一部分。 在正常的检测数据集中,前地可以覆盖超过一半的图像. 但是在人权观察的场景中,前地通常还不到15%[4],因为图像来自大型现实世界的观点,这些观点自然包括了天空,建筑物,或树木等广阔的背景区域. 这意味着探测器需要通过许多背景搜索才能找到几个目标,甚至像DINO [14],可变形DETR [35],RTT [12] 这样的强力模型也经常在背景过于主导时出错. 图1说明了这一问题。

blocks.en: Figure 1 : Comparison of RoI between different backbones. (b) SparseFormer selects a fixed ratio of regions for processing, regardless of input variability. (c) BiHashFormer combines lower selection ratio in the compression branch with dynamic compensation, making it more flexible and efficient. For the compensation branch, windows are drawn if any key in them is selected.

blocks.en: The second challenge in HRW detection is the heavy demand on computation. Many application scenarios, such as UAV inspection (VisDrone [ 2 ] ) or medical analysis (VL-Health [ 20 ] ), require detectors to respond in real time. Yet as image resolution grows—from millions of pixels in COCO [ 5 ] to billions in PANDA [ 27 ] —the processing cost rises sharply. Conventional detectors scale poorly with input size, and inference speed can drop by nearly two orders of magnitude, making real-time deployment difficult.
blocks.zh: 人权观察发现的第二个挑战是对计算的大量需求。 许多应用情景,例如无人驾驶航空器检查(VisDrone [2])或医学分析(VL-Health [20]),要求探测器实时响应. 然而,随着图像分辨率的增长——从二氧化碳[5]亿像素增长到PANDA[27]亿像素——加工成本急剧上升。 常规探测器的大小与输入大小不相称,推论速度可以下降近两个数量级,使得实时部署变得困难.

blocks.en: Thirdly, the strong interleaving of foreground and background. HRW detection often requires larger windows (in Swin [ 7 ] ) to capture sufficient context, especially in crowded scenes. Yet enlarging the window in conventional attention introduces excessive background tokens, diluting the focus on true targets. For example, a person on a lawn may be overshadowed because the cumulative attention to numerous lawn tokens exceeds that of the human body, causing facial tokens to misdirect attention and lowering detection accuracy. Furthermore, this makes small objects or those surrounded by background more likely to be excluded during RoI selection, as shown in Figure 1 .
blocks.zh: 第三,前景和背景的强烈交接。 人权观察检测往往需要更大的窗口(在斯温[7])来捕捉足够的上下文,特别是在拥挤的场景中. 然而,扩大传统注意力的窗口引入了过多的背景标志,淡化了对真正目标的关注。 例如,草坪上的人可能会被蒙上阴影,因为对众多草坪道具的累积关注超过了人体,导致面部道具误入歧途并降低检测精度. 此外,如图1所示,这使得小物体或被背景所包围的物体在罗伊选择期间更有可能被排除在外。

blocks.en: Inspired by the widespread use of hashing in computer science, we propose BiHashFormer which combines dual-branch design with hashing, achieving both sparse attention and robust compensation for overlooked targets. Firstly, a variance-based scoring mechanism ranks windows, and a learned foreground predictor determines the image-dependent proportion of RoIs. For the selected RoIs, a sparse Attention mechanism called HashAttention is introduced. This approach compresses the key-value pairs for each query, leading to finer-grained computational reduction. At the same time, the quality of attention within RoIs will be improved. In the remaining regions, detection targets are localized within the Hamming feature space obtained through hash projection. Prototype encoding is employed for this localization and such compensation can be achieved with extremely low computational cost. On PANDA [ 27 ] , BiHashFormer achieves a 37.5% reduction in FLOPs compared with SparseFormer [ 4 ] , while significantly improving AP 50 \text{AP}_{50} .
blocks.zh: 在计算机科学广泛使用散列法的启发下,我们建议波黑Former将双分支设计与散列法结合起来,对被忽略的目标既注意得很少,也给予有力的补偿。 首先,基于差异的评分机制对窗口进行排序,而学习的展望预测器则决定了RoIs的图像依赖比例. 对于所选的 RoIs,采用了一种称为"HashAttent"的稀有的注意机制. 这种方法压缩了每个查询的键值对,导致更细的加分计算还原. 同时,RoIs内部的关注质量会得到提高. 在其余区域,检测目标在通过散列投影获得的哈明地物空间内本地化. 这种本地化采用了原型编码,这种补偿可以用极低的计算成本来实现. 在PANDA[27]上,BHAashFormer与SparseFormer[4]相比实现了37.5%的FLOP,同时大幅改进了AP50\text{AP}_{50}.

blocks.en: In summary, our key contributions are:
blocks.zh: 总之,我们的主要贡献是:

blocks.en: • We propose BiHashFormer, a dual-branch vision backbone based on transformer, which combines fine-grained sparse computation with global target compensation. It is able to effectively handle sparsely distributed objects intertwined with background in HRW images while reducing computational cost. • We introduce HashAttention for the compression branch. By projecting features into a low-dimensional Hamming space, similarity computation is greatly reduced. The model compresses interactions between query and key-value pairs, achieving RoI-level sparse computation and refining attention results. • We design HashMiner for the compensation branch. In the Hamming feature space, the model learns prototype codes for detection targets, enabling retrieval of objects from non-RoI regions with minimal overhead and providing compensation for small or difficult targets. • We develop a label-free strategy with a special loss for prototype codes. Leveraging information from the compression branch, the model learns codes that capture broader and more accurate human-related semantics.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Object detection in high-resolution wide shots. High-resolution wide-shot (HRW) detection focuses on the challenge of identifying sparse targets within gigapixel-scale images. Unlike traditional benchmarks such as ImageNet [ 7 ] , HRW scenes are characterized by extremely low target density (often below 15% coverage) and highly diverse backgrounds, as highlighted in PANDA [ 27 ] . Although mainstream detectors, including Faster R-CNN [ 13 ] and Deformable Convolutional Networks [ 5 ] , perform well in dense environments, their computational burden grows rapidly with image resolution, leading to unacceptable latency. Shufflenet [ 32 ] improves efficiency by employing grouped convolutions to reduce complexity, yet it lacks mechanisms for selective computation across image regions. DynamicDet [ 6 ] introduces adaptive inference by routing inputs through different pathways based on estimated difficulty, but its binary partitioning strategy is unsuitable for HRW scenarios and the dual-branch design adds unnecessary overhead. Similarly, DGE [ 24 ] has been utilized to strengthen vision transformers, but its rigidity limits adaptability to the unique demands of HRW detection.
blocks.zh: 在高分辨率宽镜头中进行物体探测. 高分辨广射(HRW)的探测重点是在千兆像素尺度图像中识别出稀有目标的挑战. 与ImageNet等传统基准[7]不同的是,人权观察的场景的特点是目标密度极低(往往低于15%的覆盖率),背景也非常多样化,正如PANDA[27]所强调. 虽然主流的探测器,包括更快速的R-CNN [13]和可变的革命网络[5],在密集的环境中表现良好,但其计算负担随着图像分辨率而迅速增加,导致不可接受的延迟. Shufflenet[32]通过使用分组演化来降低复杂性来提高效率,然而它缺乏跨图像区域的选择性计算机制. Dot [6]根据估计的困难情况,通过不同途径输送投入,引入了适应性的推论,但其二进制分割战略不适合人权观察的设想,而双重分支设计增加了不必要的间接费用。 同样,DGE [24]也被用来加强视力变压器,但其刚性限制了对人权观察检测的独特要求的适应性。

blocks.en: Vision transformers for detection. Transformers have achieved remarkable success in the field of natural language processing (NLP) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) are likewise revolutionizing detection by modeling long-range dependencies through attention. Swin [ 7 ] mitigates the rising computational cost of large images with window-based attention, yet falls short of the contextual demands of HRW images. Dual-branch models like DBCT-Net [ 28 ] fuse global and local features but fail to extract task-relevant information from massive non-RoI regions, leading to inefficiency in HRW detection. They share a common limitation: either treat all tokens equally or focus only on selected RoIs, overlooking the small and hard targets that are prevalent in HRW scenarios.
blocks.zh: 视变器用于探测. 变形器在自然语言处理(NLP)领域取得了出众的成功,而Vision Transformers(ViTs)同样通过通过关注来建模长距离依赖性来进行革命性的检测. Swin [7] 减轻了基于窗口关注的大型图像不断上升的计算成本,但未能达到人权观察图像的背景要求. DBCT-Net[28]等双分支模型将全球和本地特征引信,但未能从大规模非国际公路运输区域提取与任务有关的信息,导致人权观察检测效率低下。 他们有一个共同的限制:要么平等对待所有物证,要么只关注选定的物证,忽略了在人权观察设想中普遍存在的小而硬的目标。

blocks.en: Sparse attention methods. To enhance the effectiveness of attention mechanisms in HRW detection, numerous sparsification approaches have been proposed. XAttention [ 13 ] leverages the sum along the anti-diagonal of the attention matrix to selectively compute more important blocks, which binds queries and key–value pairs together and limits expressiveness. Linformer [ 10 ] applies low-rank projections to compute attention in reduced dimensions, trading semantic richness for lower cost. DSA [ 22 ] attempts top - k sparsification based on attention weights from q–k dot products, but the computational overhead of the dot product itself is prohibitive in HRW scenarios.
blocks.zh: 斯派斯的注意方法。 为了提高监测站发现的注意机制的效力,已提出许多抽筋方法。 XAttention [13] 利用注意力矩阵反对角的总和有选择地计算出更重要的块,这些块将询问和键-值对结合在一起并限制表达. Linformer [10] 应用低等的预测来计算受关注度的缩小,用语义丰富的来换取更低的成本. DSA[22]尝试根据q-k点产品的注意分量进行上-k spursization,但点产品本身的计算间接费用在人权观察设想中是令人望而却步的。

blocks.en: 3.1 Overview of BiHashFormer
blocks.zh: 3.1 波黑概况

blocks.en: In the main network, input image is partitioned into non-overlapping patches of size ( H 4 × W 4 × 48 \frac{H}{4}\times\frac{W}{4}\times 48 ) where H H and W W denote the original size of input. Through linear embedding layer, the number of channel is projected into C C in the first stage. In subsequent stages, the width and height of the feature maps are progressively halved while channel doubled by merging patches, reshaping the size into ( H 8 × W 8 × 2 ​ C \frac{H}{8}\times\frac{W}{8}\times 2C ) for RoI Selector. The RoI Selector segments the feature map into w × w w\times w windows, further categorizing them into RoI and non-RoI regions based on variance, as shown in Figure 2 . RoIs are fed into the compression branch for feature extraction, which accounts for the major computational cost of the model; non-RoI regions are processed in the compensation branch, where features are first filtered and then extracted to recover information from small and hard targets. The features extracted from the two branches are directly merged. The RoI Selector together with the two branches forms a Hash Block, which serves as the basic unit of each stage. The model consists of four stages, with the number of Hash Blocks in each stage (i.e., the stage depth) set to [ 2 , 2 , 6 , 2 ] [2,2,6,2] .

RoI选择器将特性映射分入 w × w\times w 窗口,进一步根据差异将其分入RoI和非RoI区域,如图2所示. RoI被输入到压缩分支中以进行地物提取,这说明模型的主要计算成本;非RoI区域在补偿分支中处理,其中地物先被过滤出后被取出从小而硬的目标中取回信息. 从两个分会提取的特征被直接合并. blocks.en: In the compression branch, query and key will be separately projected into low dimensional Hamming space. HashAttention is then applied to RoIs window by window to extract features. Specifically, all queries participate in the attention computation, but the number of interacting key–value pairs is halved according to the Hamming distance. We illustrates the selected k-v pairs for an example query (colored red) in Figure 2 . Prototype codes is learned within this branch through ℒ p ​ r ​ o ​ t ​ o \mathcal{L}_{proto} (see Section 3.5 ). In the compensation branch, only the keys are projected. HashMiner then identifies the target-associated tokens using prototype codes and applies conventional self-attention to extract features. An example window is shown in Figure 2 .
blocks.zh: 在压缩分支中,会将查询和密钥分别投放到低维汉明空间. 然后将HashAttenty通过窗口应用到RoIs窗口来提取特性. 具体来说,所有查询都参与注意力计算,但相互作用的密钥-值对的数量根据哈明距离减半. 我们在图2中为一个示例查询(有色红色)演示选定的k-v对。 本分支内部通过L p r o t o\ mathcal{L}_{proto}(见第3.5节)学习出原型代码. 在赔偿处,只预测出钥匙。 HashMiner然后用原型代码识别出目标相關的符號并应用常规自意来提取特征. 图2显示一个示例窗口。

blocks.en: Q&K projectors. To evaluate token similarity efficiently in HRW detection, we project queries and keys into a low dimensional Hamming space. Compared with cosine similarity, its compact binary codes allow inexpensive integer operations: z = 𝐏 Q / K T ⋅ x , b = 𝟏 [ z > 0 ] \displaystyle z=\mathbf{P}_{Q/K}^{T}\cdot x,\quad b=\mathbf{1}[z>0] (9) Here x ∈ R d x\in\mathrm{R}^{d} is a query or key, 𝐏 Q / K ∈ R d × k \mathbf{P}_{Q/K}\in\mathrm{R}^{d\times k} and k = 32 k=32 . Separate Q/K projectors produce elementwise binary codes b ∈ { 0 , 1 } k b\in\{0,1\}^{k} , with zero mapped to bit 0. Gradients use the Straight-Through Estimator (STE): ∂ ℒ ∂ z = : 1 2 ​ ∂ ℒ ∂ b \frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial z}=:\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial b} (10) Notably, instead of projecting the raw tokens, we project the queries and keys. This is explained below.

Compress KV for each Q. A larger window size can better accommodate complex HRW scenarios. However, for the tokens within each window, this implies greater interference when computing attention. We expect each token to engage in attention interactions only with the tokens it truly requires. This implies that we must know what information each token needs, as well as what information it contains. This precisely corresponds to the query and key in the attention mechanism, thereby explaining why we choose them for projection.
We employ the Hamming distance to measure the similarity between keys and queries: d ​ i ​ s H ​ ( b q , b k ) = ‖ b q ⊕ b k ‖ 1 dis_{H}(b_{q},b_{k})=||b_{q}\oplus b_{k}||_{1} (11) Here ⊕ \oplus denotes bitwise XOR, and | | ⋅ | | 1 ||\cdot||_{1} represents the count of different positions. A larger Hamming distance indicates that the two vectors are farther apart in the Hamming space, implying a greater discrepancy between the information required by the query and the information contained in the key.
For a given query q q , KV Selector selects the half of the keys with the smallest Hamming distance in the window, marked as 𝐊 0.5 \mathbf{K}_{0.5} . Each value is bound to the corresponding key from the same token, and compute the HashAttention (HA) as: HA ​ ( q , 𝐊 0.5 , 𝐕 0.5 ) = softmax ​ ( q ​ 𝐊 0.5 ⊤ d key ) ​ 𝐕 0.5 \text{HA}(q,\mathbf{K}_{0.5},\mathbf{V}_{0.5})=\text{softmax}\left(\frac{q\mathbf{K}_{0.5}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_{\text{key}}}}\right)\mathbf{V}_{0.5} (12) HA is calculated in windows. Taking the case in Figure 2 as an example, we illustrate the projection results of four keys, simplified into a 2-bit form: 00, 00, 01, and 11. Considering a query projected as 11, it will select the key–value pairs corresponding to 01 and 11 (they get smaller d ​ i ​ s H dis_{H} as 1 and 0), and compute HashAttention in the original space.

blocks.en: Learning from the compression branch. Prototype codes are obtained by binarizing several trainable tokens into 0–1 representations, which need training data. Since the two branches within the same Hash Block share the key projector, the Hamming space corresponding to the keys remains consistent. As the compression branch processes RoIs that already contain rich target features, where prototype codes can be efficiently learned from. We employ the keys selected by the KV Selector to train the prototype codes, which reduces computation. Moreover, visualization experiments ( Figure 3 ) demonstrate that the selected keys contain richer target information.

blocks.en: 4.1 Datasets
blocks.zh: 4.1 数据集

blocks.en: Our primary evaluation is conducted on the PANDA [ 27 ] dataset, the first human-centric gigapixel-level benchmark featuring 13 training and 5 testing scenes with approximately 16 million annotated bounding boxes. The average image resolution of this dataset, 25,000 × \times 16,000 pixels, presents unprecedented computational demands, establishing a rigorous testbed for efficiency assessment.
blocks.zh: 我们的主要评价是在PANDA[27]数据集上进行的,这是第一个以人为中心的千兆像素水平基准,包括13个培训和5个测试场景,有大约1 600万个附加说明的边框。 这个数据集的平均图像分辨率为25,000 ×\time 16,000像素,提出了前所未有的计算需求,为效率评估建立了一个严格的测试床.

blocks.en: 4.2 Evaluation metrics
blocks.zh: 4.2 评价尺度

blocks.en: Model efficiency is quantified using FLOPs and standard COCO metrics, with particular emphasis on AP 50 \text{AP}_{50} , AP small \text{AP}_{\text{small}} ( < 96 × 96 <96\times 96 ), AP medium \text{AP}_{\text{medium}} ( 96 × 96 ∼ 288 × 288 96\times 96\sim 288\times 288 ) and AP large \text{AP}_{\text{large}} ( > 288 × 288 >288\times 288 ). We further record the FLOPs on foreground (FLOPs-F) and background (FLOPs-B) to provide a more fine - grained evaluation of model. To ensure fair comparison, all detectors process uniformly cropped 1280×800 windows from test images. Given the dynamic token selection mechanism in BiHashFormer, its FLOPs are estimated by averaging measurements across the test set. All implementations utilized the MMDetection [ 1 ] framework under standardized 36-epoch training protocols.
blocks.zh: 模型效率使用FLOP和标准COCO 度量标准进行量化,特别强调AP 50\text{AP}_{50},AP小\text{小\text{( < 96 × 96 <96\tims 96),AP中\text{中\(96 × 288 × 288\tims 96\sim 288)和AP大\text{大\text{( > 288 × 288\tims 288)). 我们进一步记录了前景FLOPs(FLOPs-F)和背景(FLOPs-B),以提供对模型的更精细的-粒化评价. 为确保公平比较,所有探测器都从测试图像中统一裁剪出1280×800个窗口。 鉴于波黑的动态符号选择机制,其FLOP是通过测试组平均测量值来估算的。 所有实施都利用了标准化的36个时代培训协议下的MM探测[1]框架。

blocks.en: 4.3 Data analysis on PANDA
blocks.zh: 4.3 (中文(简体) ). PANDA数据分析

blocks.en: As presented in Table 1 , traditional detectors consistently exceed 200 GFLOPs for backbone computation on PANDA [ 27 ] , whereas modern Transformer-based approaches like Dynamic-head [ 6 ] and DINO [ 14 ] reduces computational costs to sub-100 GFLOPs. SparseFormer achieves further reduction to 75.71 GFLOPs through fixed-ratio window selection while delivering significant AP gains.
blocks.zh: 如表1所示,传统的探测器在PANDA [27] 的骨干计算中始终超过200 GFLOP,而以Dynamic-head [6]和DINO [14]等现代变压器为基础的方法则将计算成本降低到分100 GFLOP. SparseFormer通过固定比例窗口选择进一步将GFLOP削减到75.71,同时实现显著的AP收益.

blocks.en: BiHashFormer is combined with Dynamic-head [ 6 ] and DINO [ 14 ] to evaluate its performance. The results indicate that BiHashFormer achieves superior detection performance with significantly lower computation. Compared with SparseFormer [ 4 ] , our backbone achieves a 37.5% reduction in computational cost on DINO while improving AP 50 \text{AP}_{50} by 3.85%. In comparison with Swin-T [ 7 ] , the reduction in computation reaches 64.4%. Notably, employing BiHashFormer on DINO yields a 16.34% improvement in AP small \text{AP}_{\text{small}} over SparseFormer, and this gain further increases to 55.22% on Dynamic-Head. It can be observed that the proportion of foreground computation in BiHashFormer has significantly increased, rising from 9.1% in SparseFormer to 15.43%. This indicates that our backbone achieves better efficiency.
blocks.zh: BEHashFormer与动态头[6]和DINO[14]合并,以评估其性能. 结果表明,波黑SHASFORmer的检测性能优异,计算明显较低。 与SparseFormer [4] 相比,我们的主干线实现了DINO的计算成本降低37.5%,同时将AP 50\text{AP}_{50}改进3.85%. 与Swin-T [7] 相比,计算率下降至64.4%。 值得注意的是,在DINO上使用波黑SHAashFORmer后,AP小\text{AP}_{\text{小\\}比SparseFORmer有16.34%的改善,这在动态头部上进一步提升到55.22%. 可以看出,波黑Former的预测计算比例大幅上升,从SparseFormer的9.1%上升到15.43%。 这表明我们的骨干提高了效率。

blocks.en: In addition, we record the computational cost proportion of the two branches in BiHashFormer: 38.12 GFLOPs for the compression branch and 8.29 GFLOPs for the other. It can be observed that the compression branch constitutes the major computational overhead. Although the compensation branch receives a larger input region (85% of all), it accounts for only 17.9% of the branches computation, which highlights the efficiency of HashMiner’s selection.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们还记录了波黑什Former两个分支的计算成本比例:压缩分支38.12 GFLOPs和另一分支8.29 GFLOPs. 可以看出,压缩分支构成主要的计算间接费用. 尽管补偿处得到更大的投入区(占总数的85%),但它只占分支计算量的17.9%,这凸显出Hashminer的遴选效率.

blocks.en: Further, the figure reveals an interesting pattern: queries from the head tend to interact with key–value pairs covering the entire body, whereas queries from the body and background focus more on the key–value pairs located at the boundary between foreground and background. This may be because the head, as a key marker of a person, serves as a suitable anchor for feature extraction, linking other parts of the body to form the entirety of the detection target. In contrast, the body and the surrounding environment focus more on differences, assisting the backbone in distinguishing between target and background features. blocks.en: 4.5 Study on the compensation branch
blocks.zh: 4.5 关于赔偿部门的研究

blocks.en: Necessity of the compensation branch. Since the model requires at least one inference pathway and the compression branch serves as the main branch of BiHashFormer, we conduct an ablation study on the alternative compensation branch. First, we disabled this branch during inference. Although this reduced its computational cost, it significantly degraded detection performance, particularly for small objects, as evidenced by nearly a 51.4% drop in AP small \text{AP}_{\text{small}} in Table X3 in the supplementary material.
blocks.zh: 赔偿处的必要性。 由于该模型至少需要一条推论路径,压缩分支是波黑什福尔默的主要分支,因此我们对替代补偿分支进行消化研究。 首先,我们在推论中 使这个分支失效 虽然这降低了其计算成本,但检测性能显著下降,特别是小物体的检测性能,从补充材料表X3中的AP small\text{AP}_{\text{ small}}}的AP small\text 下降近51.4%即可证明.

blocks.en: Subsequently, we replaced this branch with a classical attention module for feature compensation. Specifically, the entire image was first down-sampled via average pooling with a reduction factor equal to the window size w w . Attention computation was then performed on the down-sampled image, and the results from non-RoI regions were mapped back to the original resolution, forming a complete feature map together with the features obtained from the compression branch. This ensures that the compression branch remains unaffected while keeping the computational cost of the replacement comparable to the compensation branch. We define the efficiency as following to demonstrate the efficiency of different methods in compensating features for small objects, where AP small NA \text{AP}_{\text{small}}^{\text{NA}} refers to the 0.287 in Table X3: Eff = 100 ⋅ ( AP small − AP small NA ) / GFLOPs \text{Eff}=100\cdot(\text{AP}_{\text{small}}-\text{AP}_{\text{small}}^{\text{NA}})/\text{GFLOPs} (17)
blocks.zh: 之后,我们用一个典型的注意单元来取代这个分支,用于特征补偿. 具体地说,整个图像首先通过平均集合进行下采样,还原系数等于窗口大小ww. 随后在被下取样的图像上进行了注意计算,从非RoI区域得到的结果被映射回原分辨率,与从压缩分支得到的特性一起组成了完整的地物映射. 这样可以确保压缩处不受影响,同时保持替换的计算成本与补偿处的可比性. 我们对效率的定义如下,以显示在小对象补偿特性方面不同方法的效率,其中AP small NA\text{AP}_{\text{ small}}^{\text{NA}}}指表X3中的0.287: Eff = 100⋅ (AP small-AP small NA) / GFLOPs\text{Eff}=100\cdot(\text{AP}_{\t{-\\textext{ small}}^{\t}}{NA}}}/\text{GFLOPs} (17)

blocks.en: These two ablation experiments demonstrate the necessity of the compensation branch: it cannot be replaced by simple feature extraction methods, nor can it be directly removed.
blocks.zh: 这两起衰减实验证明了补偿分支的必要性:它不能被简单的特征提取方法所取而代之,也不能被直接去除.

blocks.en: Selection methods compared with HashMiner. We aim to determine whether the effect brought by HashMiner is truly efficient or merely redundant. To this end, we experimented with several alternative selection methods and focused on comparing their computational cost, latency and AP small \text{AP}_{\text{small}} .
blocks.zh: 与Hashminer相比的选取方法. 我们的目的是确定Hashminer带来的效果是否真正有效,还是仅仅是多余的。 为此,我们尝试了几种备选选择方法,并侧重于比较它们的计算成本、耐用性和AP小\text{AP}_{\text{小}。

blocks.en: The results in Table X1 show that whether using random selection, training a simple MLP to decide selection, or leveraging gradient-based criteria, none of these approaches outperform HashMiner in compensating features for small objects, proved by AP small \text{AP}_{\text{small}} . Moreover, both computational cost and latency remaining well-controlled on HashMiner.

To handle the more complex scenarios and larger scale variations in HRW shots, we increase the window size, thereby allowing attention interactions among tokens to cover a broader range. blocks.en: 4.7 Supplementary experiments
blocks.zh: 4.7 补充实验

blocks.en: Section 2 of the supplementary material reports inference latency, DOTA/VisDrone generalization, and STE training stability. On COCO, BiHashFormer with Mask R-CNN and a 3 × 3\times schedule reaches 48.3 AP using three prototypes, versus 46.0 for Swin-T, with 35.6% fewer backbone/neck FLOPs. Across 80 categories, three prototypes give the best accuracy among the tested counts, supporting class-agnostic foreground retrieval. With the same DINO head, BiHashFormer reaches 0.810 AP 50 \text{AP}_{50} at 47.31 GFLOPs and 2.8 s, outperforming the complete Linformer and XAttention configurations. With matched DINOv3 [ 9 ] ViT-S+/16 initialization and 36-epoch training, it gains 4.0 AP 50 \text{AP}_{50} and 11.6 AP small \text{AP}_{\text{small}} points over the baseline with 64.4% fewer FLOPs. On eight RTX 4090 GPUs with one image per GPU, training takes 19.7 h versus SparseFormer’s 23.2 h and reaches 0.75 AP 50 \text{AP}_{50} five epochs earlier. Full protocols and results appear in supplementary Tables X9–X13.
blocks.zh: 补充材料报告第2节:推断延迟、DOTA/VisDrone通用和STE培训稳定性。 在COCO上,带有Mask R-CNN的波黑Former以及3×3\时段时间表使用3个原型达到了48.3AP,而Swin-T的为46.0,骨干/颈部FLOP减少了35.6%. 在80个类别中,3个原型在被测试的计数中给出了最好的准确度,支持类不可知的前地检索. 使用相同的DINO头,BHAashFormer在47.31 GFLOPs和2.8 s达到0.810 AP 50\text{AP}_{50},比完整的Linformer和XAttenting配置要好. 通过匹配的 DINov3 [9] VIT-S+/16 初始化和36个时代的训练,它获得了4.0 AP 50\text{AP}_{50} 和 11.6 AP small\text{AP}_{\text{ small}}Q}} 的分数,比基线少64.4% FLOP. 训练需要19.7小时与SparseFormer的23.2小时, 完整的协议和结果见补充表X9–X13.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: By deeply integrating hashing concepts with object detection, we propose BiHashFormer, a dual-branch vision transformer. It employs RoI Selector to sparsely select RoI, leverages Hamming distance to refine the attention mechanism into a sparsified HashAttention and utilizes HashMiner to dynamically compensate for object features in non-RoI regions. Thereby it reduces FLOPs by 64.4% versus Swin-T [ 7 ] and 37.5% versus SparseFormer [ 4 ] while achieving 81.0% AP 50 \text{AP}_{50} on PANDA [ 27 ] . This dual-branch paradigm establishes a new standard for efficient large-scale vision systems, particularly for real-time applications with constrained resources.
blocks.zh: 通过将散列概念与物体探测深度结合起来,我们提议采用波黑SHASFORmer,一种双分支视觉变压器。 它使用RoI Selector来稀少地选择RoI,利用Hamming距离来将注意力机制精炼成被垃圾桶化的HashAttenty,并利用HashMiner来动态地补偿非RoI地区的物体特征. 由此,在PANDA上实现了81.0%的AP 50\text{AP}_{50}的FLOP对Swin-T [7] 和37.5%对SparseFormer [4] 减少64.4%. 这种双重分支模式为高效的大规模愿景系统,特别是资源有限的实时应用确立了新的标准。

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The main claims can accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The reason behind a pattern in section 4.4 need further investigation. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The proof is correct. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Hyper-parameters are given. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [No] Justification: Codes in PyTorch are given in the supplementary material. But the complete code has not been released yet. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: They are in the section 4. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Some experiments take the average value of many runs. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: AGX Orin and RTX 4090 are used. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We reviewed the guidelines and found no conflicts. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: They are both discussed. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: N/A Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: All reused assets are cited with their sources. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: New assets are not released yet. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: N/A Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: N/A Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [N/A] Justification: N/A Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 说明: 主要索赔可以准确地反映文件的贡献和范围。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明: 第4.4节模式背后的原因需要进一步调查。 • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应反思这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果该办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响该方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[是] 说明: 证相正相. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 · 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 说明:给出了超参数。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大型语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示? 答: [否]说明:PyTorch中的代码在补充材料中给出. 但完整代码尚未发布. · 答案[N/A]是指纸张不包括需要密码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 文件不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). 二. 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何取用原始数据、预处理后的数据、中间数据和生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本来复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从剧本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用的话)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的资料(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(例如数据分解、超参数、如何选择、优化者类型等)? 答复:[是] 说明: 它们载于第4节,准则:答案[不适用/A]意味着该文件不包括实验。 试验环境应在文件的核心中详细介绍,以便评估结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过守则、附录或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 一些实验采用了许多跑道的平均值. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布式错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-西格玛出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格. 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 说明:使用了AGX Orin和RTX 4090。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额并估计总计算数。 文件应披露整个研究项目是否比文件所报道的实验需要更多的计算(例如,初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写入文件)。 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复: [是] 理由: 我们审查了准则,没有发现冲突。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和负面社会影响? 答复:[是] 说明: 二者都经过讨论。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件不讨论社会影响。 二. 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(如:造谣、制造假相、监视)、公平考虑(如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以使人们能训练出能更快地生成Deepfake的模型. ^ 作者应考虑在技术被作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术被作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而可能造成的损害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行严格公布,在攻击之外提供防御,监测滥用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布滥用风险高的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或被刮去的数据集)而采取的保障措施? 答复:[无/A] 理由说明:无/A准则: 答复[无/A]意味着该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放有可能被滥用或双重用途的已释放模型时,应采取必要的保障措施,允许控制地使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。 二. 支助 从互联网上取出的数据组可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明他们如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点并作出最真诚的努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有者,是否适当记名,是否明确提到并适当遵守许可证和使用条件? 答复:[是] 说明: 所有再利用的资产都与来源一起列出。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用了哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证的名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应当包括每项资产. 二. 支助 对于某一来源(如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产被放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于受欢迎的数据集,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 他们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 二. 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果不在网上提供这种信息,鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,与资产一起提供的文件是否充分? 答复:[不详]理由: 新资产尚未释放。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放出新的资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板通报数据集/代码/模型的细节,作为其提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 文件应讨论是否以及如何从资产被使用的人那里获得同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL , 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 与人类主题有关的众包和研究 关于与人类主体的众包实验和研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示和(如果适用的话)截图的全文,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 回答:[N/A] 理由说明:n/A 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人主体的研究. • 将这些资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果文件的主要贡献涉及人类课题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 二. 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少领取数据收集国的最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于涉及人类课题的研究。 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向研究对象披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得的同等批准/审查)? 回答:[N/A] 理由说明:n/A 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人主体的研究. • 研究对象的研究可能需要IRB批准(或同等批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在文件中明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大相径庭,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 二. 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包含任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如果适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。 16. LLM使用宣言问题: 论文是否描述了LLMS的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作、编辑或格式化目的,而且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要申报。 答复:[无/A] 理由说明:有/A 准则: 答案[无/A]是指本研究中的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]

blocks.en: Justification: The main claims can accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope.
blocks.zh: 说明: 主要索赔可以准确地反映文件的贡献和范围。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The reason behind a pattern in section 4.4 need further investigation.
blocks.zh: 说明: 第4.4节模式背后的原因需要进一步调查。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. blocks.en: Experiment statistical significance
blocks.zh: 实验统计意义

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?
blocks.zh: 问题: 纸质报告错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息?

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed?

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. blocks.en: We trained BiHashFormer with ten randomly drawn seeds and evaluated them on PANDA. Thanks to the binary nature of hash encoding, each pre-hash coordinate z z only needs to preserve its sign, rather than taking continuous integer values as in quantization. GFLOPs-O covers the backbone and neck at an input resolution of 1333 × 800 1333\times 800 , consistent with the computational scope used in the main paper. blocks.en: The Hamming dimension and prototype count serve different purposes. The 32-bit space encodes distinctions among categories, instances, and object parts, while the prototypes provide class-agnostic retrieval anchors for foreground structures. HashAttention uses binary codes to select key–value pairs and computes attention with their original continuous features. HashMiner uses the prototypes to retrieve missed foreground tokens, and the detection head predicts their categories. A prototype therefore need not correspond to a single object class.

blocks.en: 2.5 Comparison with efficient attention methods
blocks.zh: 2.5 与高效关注方法的比较

blocks.en: We compare complete Linformer [ 10 ] , XAttention [ 13 ] , SparseFormer [ 4 ] , and BiHashFormer model configurations on PANDA, each paired with the same DINO detection head [ 14 ] . Table X10 reports backbone/neck GFLOPs, inference latency, and detection accuracy for these full configurations.
blocks.zh: 我们比较了PANDA上的完整的Linformer [10],XAtentent [13],SparseFormer [4],和波黑Former模型配置,每个配置都与相同的DINO检测头 [14]. 表X10报告了主干/颈部GFLOP、推断延缓性和这些完整配置的检测准确性。

blocks.en: Linformer projects the key and value sequences to a fixed rank before computing attention. This compression can mix weak small-object features with background features. HashAttention instead uses low-dimensional Hamming codes for query-specific selection and computes attention using the selected continuous features. XAttention estimates block importance through antidiagonal scoring. Its reported acceleration targets sequences of 8k–256k tokens, whereas a 21 × 21 21\times 21 window in our model contains 441 tokens. At this scale, block selection is coarser and its overhead is harder to amortize. BiHashFormer also uses HashMiner to recover target-related tokens outside the selected RoIs.
blocks.zh: Linformer在计算注意力前将密钥和值序列投放到固定的级别. 这种压缩可以将弱小对象特征与背景特征相混合. 取而代之的是,HashAttenty使用低维汉明代码进行查询特定选择,并使用所选连续特性计算注意. X注意估计通过反对角分数阻断了重要性. 它的加速目标序列为8k–256k令牌,而我们模型中21×21 21\时21个窗口包含441个令牌. 在这个尺度上,块的选择比较紧凑,其间接费用更难摊还. 波黑什 前作还使用HashMiner来取回所选 RoIs以外的与目标相关的符号.

blocks.en: 2.6 Evaluation with DINOv3 pretraining
blocks.zh: 2.6 用DINOv3预训进行评价

blocks.en: The main-paper PANDA results use training from scratch. To evaluate the method with strong pretrained features, we initialize both models in Table X11 from the same official DINOv3 ViT-S+/16 checkpoint [ 9 ] and train for 36 epochs. ViT-S+/16 has 12 blocks and approximately 29 million parameters, close to the 12-block Swin-T/BiHashFormer configuration. Both models use identical input resolution, augmentation, optimizer, batch size, detector, losses, and evaluation settings.
blocks.zh: 主论文"PANDA"结果从零开始使用训练. 为了评价该方法具有很强的先行性能,我们从同名官方的DINOv3 VIT-S+/16检查站中初始化了表X11中的两种型号[9],为36个纪元的列车. ViT-S+/16有12个块和约2900万个参数,接近12个块的Swin-T/BiHashFormer配置. 这两个模型都使用相同的输入分辨率,增强,优化,批量大小,检测器,损失,以及评价设置.

blocks.en: We group the single-resolution ViT blocks as [ 2 , 2 , 6 , 2 ] [2,2,6,2] without downsampling. Within each block, the RoI Selector routes ranked spatial windows to HashAttention or HashMiner. The class token and four register tokens remain global and bypass this routing.
